_source: Transcribed word for word from Ella Docs, "Curriculum & Skills Mapping" (ella.navgurukul.org/curriculum), by way of Ella Mobile's supabase/functions/ella/curriculum.ts. Each skill's short label is ours. Read by the Rust backend (src-tauri/src/curriculum.rs) and the browser preview (src/lib/curriculum.ts).

levels.name: Pre-Beginner
levels.goal: I can talk about myself and things around me.

steps.title: First words
steps.focus: Naming the things I can see.

skills.label: Colours, numbers
skills.text: I can name colours and say numbers 1–10.

skills.label: Everyday things
skills.text: I can name familiar animals and everyday objects at school and home.

skills.label: A and the
skills.text: I can use ‘a’ and ‘the’ in a simple phrase — a cat, the bag.

skills.label: Naming things
skills.text: I can name things in English when someone points at them.

steps.title: I am and I have got
steps.focus: Saying who I am and what I have.

skills.label: About me
skills.text: I can say my name, my age, and the name of my school and family members.

skills.label: Saying I am
skills.text: I can say ‘I am’ and ‘I am not’ — I am happy. I am not tired.

skills.label: I have got
skills.text: I can use ‘I have got’ — I have got a dog. I haven’t got a sister.

skills.label: Introducing myself
skills.text: I can introduce myself in English in a few short phrases.

steps.title: I like and I don’t like
steps.focus: Saying what I enjoy — and what I don’t.

skills.label: Things I like
skills.text: I can name things I like — food, sports, animals, colours.

skills.label: Likes and dislikes
skills.text: I can say ‘I like’ and ‘I don’t like’ — I like cricket. I don’t like eggs.

skills.label: Joining with and
skills.text: I can use ‘and’ to join two things — I like cats and dogs.

skills.label: Full answers
skills.text: I can answer ‘Do you like…?’ with a short sentence, not just yes or no.

steps.title: I can
steps.focus: Saying what I am able to do.

skills.label: Positions
skills.text: I can name positions — on, in, under, next to, behind.

skills.label: Can and can't
skills.text: I can use ‘can’ to say what someone is able to do — I can run. She can’t fly.

skills.label: Where things are
skills.text: I can say where things are — The bag is on the chair. There is a pen on the table.

skills.label: My abilities
skills.text: I can answer ‘What can you do?’ with a simple sentence.

steps.title: What is happening?
steps.focus: Using present continuous and putting it all together in a short exchange.

skills.label: Right now
skills.text: I can use present continuous for right now — She is running. They are eating.

skills.label: What I'm doing
skills.text: I can answer questions in the present — What are you doing? I am reading.

skills.label: Short exchanges
skills.text: I can keep a simple exchange going for 2–3 turns on a familiar topic.

skills.label: Keeping going
skills.text: I can keep going even when I only have a few words.

levels.name: First Words
levels.goal: I can have simple conversations on everyday topics.

steps.title: Describing the world
steps.focus: Moving from naming things to describing them.

skills.label: Describing people
skills.text: I can describe what people look like and how they feel using simple adjectives.

skills.label: Happening now
skills.text: I can use the present continuous to describe what is happening now — She is running.

skills.label: Describing places
skills.text: I can describe a picture or a place using 3–4 connected sentences.

steps.title: Talking about the past
steps.focus: Starting to use past tense to share what happened.

skills.label: Past time words
skills.text: I can use past time expressions — yesterday, last week, a long time ago.

skills.label: Regular past
skills.text: I can use past simple with regular verbs — I walked, I watched, I played.

skills.label: Irregular past
skills.text: I can use some irregular past verbs — I went, I saw, I ate, I had.

skills.label: What I did
skills.text: I can talk about something I did recently in a few connected sentences.

steps.title: Giving opinions and reasons
steps.focus: Beginning to say what I think and why.

skills.label: Opinion words
skills.text: I can use simple opinion words — I think, I feel, I prefer, I love, I hate.

skills.label: Using because
skills.text: I can use ‘because’ to give a reason — I like cricket because it’s exciting.

skills.label: Using but
skills.text: I can use ‘but’ to show contrast — I like football but not swimming.

skills.label: Opinion and reason
skills.text: I can share a simple opinion and give at least one reason for it.

steps.title: Talking about plans
steps.focus: Extending into the future — making and sharing plans.

skills.label: How often
skills.text: I can use frequency words — always, usually, sometimes, never, often.

skills.label: Future time words
skills.text: I can use future time expressions — tomorrow, next week, soon, one day.

skills.label: Going to
skills.text: I can use ‘going to’ to talk about a plan — I’m going to study tonight.

skills.label: My plans
skills.text: I can talk about what I am going to do and give a simple reason why.

steps.title: Holding a real conversation
steps.focus: Using everything together in a real back-and-forth.

skills.label: Sequence words
skills.text: I can use connecting phrases — first, then, after that, in the end.

skills.label: Mixing tenses
skills.text: I can use present simple, present continuous, and past simple together in a story.

skills.label: Back and forth
skills.text: I can hold a short back-and-forth conversation on a familiar topic without long pauses.

skills.label: Pushing through
skills.text: I can keep going even when I’m not 100% sure of every word.

levels.name: Finding My Voice
levels.goal: I can share my opinions and tell stories in English.

steps.title: Finding better words
steps.focus: Moving from words that work to words that feel right.

skills.label: Describing words
skills.text: I can use a wider range of descriptive words to make my ideas more interesting.

skills.label: Idioms
skills.text: I can understand and use common idioms I hear regularly.

skills.label: Present perfect
skills.text: I can use present perfect to connect past and present — I’ve lived here for 3 years.

skills.label: Rephrasing
skills.text: I can express an idea in more than one way when I’m not sure of a word.

steps.title: Talking about the past with more precision
steps.focus: Describing not just what happened, but what was happening and what used to be.

skills.label: Contrast words
skills.text: I can use sequence and contrast words — however, although, even though.

skills.label: Past continuous
skills.text: I can use past continuous with past simple — I was eating when she called.

skills.label: Used to
skills.text: I can use ‘used to’ to talk about past habits.

skills.label: Telling a story
skills.text: I can tell a story that moves naturally between past and present.

steps.title: Expressing opinions with depth
steps.focus: Moving from simple opinions to supported arguments.

skills.label: Opinion phrases
skills.text: I can use reporting words — I think, I believe, in my opinion, it seems to me.

skills.label: First conditional
skills.text: I can use first conditional — If I study hard, I will pass.

skills.label: Modal verbs
skills.text: I can use modal verbs — might, could, should, must — with reasonable accuracy.

skills.label: Reason and example
skills.text: I can give an opinion, support it with a reason, and add an example.

steps.title: Speaking for longer without losing the thread
steps.focus: Building up to a full minute of organised, connected speech.

skills.label: Linking words
skills.text: I can use linking adverbials — as a result, in addition, on the other hand.

skills.label: Relative clauses
skills.text: I can use relative clauses to add detail — the person who, the place where.

skills.label: One-minute talk
skills.text: I can speak for about 1 minute on a familiar topic without stopping.

skills.label: Organising ideas
skills.text: I can organise what I say so others can follow my thinking easily.

steps.title: Handling unpredictable conversations
steps.focus: Communicating flexibly in varied situations.

skills.label: Formal and casual
skills.text: I can use formal and informal vocabulary depending on who I’m talking to.

skills.label: Accurate tenses
skills.text: I can use a range of tenses together accurately in an extended story or explanation.

skills.label: Switching topics
skills.text: I can switch between topics in a conversation without losing the thread.

skills.label: Joining in
skills.text: I feel comfortable joining a conversation I didn’t prepare for.

levels.name: Speaking Freely
levels.goal: I can speak for about a minute on many different topics.

steps.title: Precision in vocabulary
steps.focus: Choosing more exact and sophisticated words.

skills.label: Precise words
skills.text: I can use a wider range of vocabulary including less common and more precise words.

skills.label: Collocations
skills.text: I can use collocations naturally — make a decision, pay attention, take a risk.

skills.label: Second conditional
skills.text: I can use second conditional fluently — If I had more time, I would travel more.

skills.label: Complex ideas
skills.text: I can express a complex idea clearly without simplifying it too much.

steps.title: Using complex grammar naturally
steps.focus: Using third conditional, reported speech, and hedging language with confidence.

skills.label: Hedging
skills.text: I can use hedging language — it could be argued, there is some evidence that.

skills.label: Third conditional
skills.text: I can use third conditional — If I had studied harder, I would have passed.

skills.label: Reported speech
skills.text: I can use reported speech fluidly — She said she would come. He asked if I was okay.

skills.label: Complex sentences
skills.text: I can use complex sentences without losing the main point.

steps.title: Speaking at length with coherence
steps.focus: Building extended, well-organised spoken responses.

skills.label: Discourse markers
skills.text: I can use discourse markers to organise speech — right, so, as I was saying, anyway.

skills.label: Passive and active
skills.text: I can use passive and active voice flexibly depending on what I want to emphasise.

skills.label: Talking at length
skills.text: I can speak for 3–5 minutes on a topic I care about with clear structure.

skills.label: Staying coherent
skills.text: I can keep a conversation coherent even when the topic shifts.

steps.title: Arguing and persuading
steps.focus: Moving from sharing opinions to defending and challenging ideas.

skills.label: Argument words
skills.text: I can use vocabulary for argumentation — claim, evidence, argue, counter, support.

skills.label: Building arguments
skills.text: I can use a range of linking devices to build structured arguments.

skills.label: Cleft sentences
skills.text: I can use cleft sentences for emphasis — What I mean is… It was she who…

skills.label: Disagreeing well
skills.text: I can challenge someone’s opinion respectfully and explain my own position clearly.

steps.title: Natural, spontaneous fluency
steps.focus: Speaking without noticeable effort on a wide range of topics.

skills.label: Registers
skills.text: I can use different registers — casual, formal, persuasive — depending on context.

skills.label: Accurate grammar
skills.text: I can use all B2 grammar structures accurately with very few errors.

skills.label: Spontaneous talk
skills.text: I can speak naturally and spontaneously on almost any familiar topic.

skills.label: Being myself
skills.text: I feel like English is a tool I can rely on to express who I really am.

levels.name: Almost Fluent
levels.goal: I feel comfortable talking with peers about complex things.

steps.title: Choosing words with more precision and feeling
steps.focus: Moving from a large vocabulary to a sensitive one — words chosen for effect, not just meaning.

skills.label: Academic words
skills.text: I can use sophisticated vocabulary across academic and professional contexts.

skills.label: Abstract words
skills.text: I can use abstract vocabulary fluently — paradox, implication, integrity, legacy.

skills.label: Inversion
skills.text: I can use inversion for emphasis naturally — Rarely have I heard such an argument.

skills.label: Nuanced ideas
skills.text: I can express nuanced ideas, not just basic ones.

steps.title: Complex grammar with ease
steps.focus: Using advanced grammar without effort or hesitation.

skills.label: Nominalisation
skills.text: I can use nominalisation to compress meaning — the rise in, the failure to act.

skills.label: Modal perfects
skills.text: I can use all modal perfects — should have, could have, might have — appropriately.

skills.label: Noun phrases
skills.text: I can use complex noun phrases and participle clauses fluently.

skills.label: Clear and complex
skills.text: I can produce complex sentences that are still clear and easy to follow.

steps.title: Sustained, coherent discourse
steps.focus: Holding the floor for extended periods.

skills.label: Fluent linking
skills.text: I can use linking adverbials and discourse markers fluently — consequently, nevertheless.

skills.label: Substitution
skills.text: I can use reference and substitution to avoid repetition across long stretches of speech.

skills.label: Extended talk
skills.text: I can speak for several minutes on any topic, organising ideas clearly as I go.

skills.label: Holding my own
skills.text: I can hold my own in academic and professional discussions.

steps.title: Register flexibility
steps.focus: Adapting instantly to any speaking context or audience.

skills.label: Mixing styles
skills.text: I can use figurative, idiomatic, and formal vocabulary naturally in the same conversation.

skills.label: Emphasis and style
skills.text: I can use a range of emphatic and stylistic structures — clefts, fronting, ellipsis.

skills.label: Shifting register
skills.text: I can shift instantly from casual conversation to formal debate without effort.

steps.title: Speaking with real precision and effect
steps.focus: Language that creates the exact effect the student intends — in any situation.

skills.label: Irony and humour
skills.text: I can use vocabulary to convey attitude, irony, humour, and subtle meaning.

skills.label: Self-correcting
skills.text: My grammar is essentially accurate — errors are rare, minor, and self-corrected.

skills.label: Skilled speaking
skills.text: I can communicate complex ideas with the precision and confidence of a skilled speaker.

skills.label: Feeling natural
skills.text: I feel completely natural when speaking English in any situation.

levels.name: Fluent
levels.goal: I can communicate on any topic with accuracy, flexibility, and no hesitation.

steps.title: Mastery of vocabulary
steps.focus: Moving towards native-level vocabulary range and sensitivity.

skills.label: Creative words
skills.text: I can use vocabulary with the precision and creativity of a skilled writer.

skills.label: Cultural fit
skills.text: I can understand and produce language with perfect register and cultural fit.

skills.label: Literary grammar
skills.text: I can use grammatical structures from literary and formal English fluently.

skills.label: Any idea
skills.text: I can communicate any idea I have in English — complex, emotional, abstract, creative.

steps.title: Grammar as craft
steps.focus: Using grammar not just accurately but artistically.

skills.label: Poetic language
skills.text: I can use figurative, symbolic, and poetic language naturally.

skills.label: Stylistic effects
skills.text: I can use grammar to create stylistic effects — rhythm, emphasis, contrast.

skills.label: Formal structures
skills.text: I can use any grammatical structure found in formal writing or oratory.

skills.label: Off the cuff
skills.text: I can produce extended, well-structured discourse without any preparation.

steps.title: Full communicative range
steps.focus: Handling any conversation, audience, or register effortlessly.

skills.label: Allusions
skills.text: I can understand cultural allusions, literary references, and historical vocabulary.

skills.label: Complex passives
skills.text: I can use all forms of reported speech, conditionals, and complex passives naturally.

skills.label: Native speakers
skills.text: I can follow and fully engage with native speakers in any context.

skills.label: Taking the floor
skills.text: I can manage multiparty conversations and take the floor with skill.

steps.title: Language as identity
steps.focus: English feels like yours — not a language you learned, but one you live in.

skills.label: Word instinct
skills.text: I can use English vocabulary with the same instinct and feeling as in my first language.

skills.label: Automatic grammar
skills.text: My grammar is fully automatic — I communicate through it, not with it.

skills.label: English as mine
skills.text: I feel that English is not a foreign language — it is simply a language I speak.

steps.title: Full mastery
steps.focus: Arriving at the highest level of English proficiency.

skills.label: Native vocabulary
skills.text: I have mastery of English vocabulary equal to a highly educated native speaker.

skills.label: Full command
skills.text: I have complete command of English grammar in all contexts and styles.

skills.label: Full expression
skills.text: I can communicate with precision, warmth, authority, and creativity in English.

skills.label: No barriers
skills.text: Language is no longer a barrier — it is a bridge to everything.
